questions.question_text: Which of these expressions is a monic quadratic trinomial?

options.why: It is a quadratic trinomial, but the coefficient of $x^2$ is $3$, so it is not monic.
It is monic and quadratic, but it has only two terms, so it is not a trinomial.
Its highest power is $x^3$ and it has four terms, so it is cubic, not a quadratic trinomial.

questions.solution_text:
A monic quadratic trinomial has three terms, highest power $x^2$, and coefficient $1$ on $x^2$.
$x^2-7x+10$ meets all three conditions.

questions.question_text: Which factor pair is needed to factorise $x^2+11x+28$?

options.why: Multiplies to $28$ but adds to $16$, not to the required sum of $11$.
Multiplies to $28$ but adds to $29$, not to the required sum of $11$.
Adds to $-11$ rather than $+11$; the constant $+28$ with a positive $11x$ needs both numbers positive.

questions.solution_text:
Product $=28$, sum $=11$
Factor pairs of $28$: $1$ and $28$, $2$ and $14$, $4$ and $7$
$4+7=11$
The pair is $4$ and $7$.

questions.question_text:
The factorisation of $x^2+4x-45$ begins with the bracket $(x+9)$.
What is the second bracket?

options.why: Gives a constant term of $+45$ instead of the required $-45$.
Used the coefficient of $x$ as the second number instead of dividing the constant by $9$.
Subtracted $9$ from $45$ instead of dividing $-45$ by $9$.

questions.solution_text:
Product $=-45$, sum $=4$
Factor pair: $9$ and $-5$
$x^2+4x-45$
$=(x+9)(x-5)$
The second bracket is $(x-5)$.

questions.question_text: When $x^2-9x+20$ is factorised into two brackets, what are the signs of the two numbers?

options.why: Two positive numbers give a positive middle term, $+9x$, not $-9x$.
Opposite signs multiply to a negative constant, but the constant here is $+20$.

questions.solution_text:
The constant $+20$ is positive, so the two numbers have the same sign.
The coefficient $-9$ is negative, so that common sign is negative.
Both numbers are negative.

questions.question_text: For which of these values of $k$ can $x^2+kx+18$ be factorised into two brackets with integer terms?

options.why: No integer factor pair of $18$ adds to $8$; the nearest pair, $3$ and $6$, adds to $9$.
No integer factor pair of $18$ adds to $13$; $2$ and $9$ adds to $11$ and $1$ and $18$ adds to $19$.
No integer factor pair of $18$ adds to $5$; the smallest positive sum available is $9$.

questions.solution_text:
Factor pairs of $18$ and their sums:
$1$ and $18$: sum $19$
$2$ and $9$: sum $11$
$3$ and $6$: sum $9$
$k=11$ gives $x^2+11x+18=(x+2)(x+9)$
